contexts.text: When intellectual things are vastated... as to goods, they are called a pasture of flocks (); so that there is no Rational.
They see falsities as truths, and truths as falsities, and thus destroy the good pasture... ().

For thy servants have no pasture for their flock () = that there are lacking scientifics in which are the goods of truth; (for) the pasture which is for the flock = the scientifics in which are the goods of truth... In the internal sense, pasture = that which supports the spiritual life, and is especially scientific truth; for this the soul of man longs, as the body does for food... and therefore to feed = to be instructed.
The stags have not found pasture () = the natural affections without truths and their goods. That pasture = truth and the good of truth, which support the spiritual life of man. References.
Pastures of herb () = spiritual nourishment, which is that of the soul; and therefore it is said, my soul he will recreate.
Ky the pasture which they have not () is signified that there is no truth in which to be instructed.
To find pasture () = to be taught, illustrated, and nourished with Divine truths.
Their pasture () = the Knowledges of truth and good.
The flock of My pasture () = spiritual good and truth; pasture = their reception by the Lord.
The pastures of the wilderness are dried up () = no spiritual nourishment in such a Church.
Pastures of herb = the Knowledges of truth and good.
A pasture of flocks = the nourishment of evil by falsities; (thus) the devastation of truth by means of falsities.
In these passages, to feed = to instruct in truths; and pasture, the truths in which they are instructed.
By the good pasture is signified all that which nourishes spiritually, especially the Word, and the derivative Knowledges of truth and good.
Pastures = the Knowledges of good and truth from the Word, because they feed the lower mind.
